Heard Ms.Anupama learned counsel who represents Sri.Girish B Baladare learned counsel for the appellants as well as Sri.H.C.Vrushabendraiah learned counsel for respondent No.1 Insurance Company.

2. The mother, father and elder sister of the deceased Ravikumar.C.M. (hereinafter be referred to as the 'deceased' NC: 2024:KHC:37448 for brevity) filed a petition seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- on the ground that the deceased died in a road traffic accident.

The Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Hassan which dealt with the matter as MVC No.873/2022, passed orders on 02.09.2023 holding that the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.23,89,000/- as compensation.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Hassan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Dissatisfied with the same, the claimants are before this Court.
3. Ms.Anupama representing the appellants contends that the deceased as an agriculturist and driver was earning Rs.30,000/- per month by the date of accident.
He was contributing his entire earnings towards the welfare of the appellants.
However, taking the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month, the Tribunal awarded a meagre sum as compensation and therefore, the appeal is filed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel also states that the accident occurred in the year 2022 and for the relevant period the Karnataka State Legal Services Authorities is taking notional income as Rs.15,500/- per month and atleast the said figure should have been considered by the Tribunal.
Learned counsel Sri.H.C.Vrushabendraiah who is representing respondent No.1 Insurance Company did not raise any objection for taking the notional income as Rs.15,500/- per month.
Also the request made appears justifiable.

6. Taking the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- per month, without disturbing the other parameters i.e., adding 40% of the earnings towards future prospects as the deceased was aged about 24 years by the date of accident, deducting 50% of the earnings towards personal and living expenses which the deceased would have occurred for himself had he been alive as the deceased died as bachelor and apply appropriate multiplier '18', the amount which the appellants are entitled to under the head loss of dependency is as under:
Amount Description In Rs.
 Notional monthly income 15,500-00  Annual Income (15,500X12) 1,86,000-00  Add 40% towards future  2,60,400-00  prospects (1,86,000/- + 40%)
 Deduct 50% towards personal  1,30,200-00  and living expenses
Applying appropriate multiplier 23,43,600-00 '18' NC: 2024:KHC:37448 7.
Thus, the amount which the appellants are entitled to under the head loss of dependency is Rs.23,43,600/-.
Together with the said amount, the appellants are entitled to Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate.
Also appellant Nos.1 & 2 being the parents of the deceased are entitled to Rs.44,000/- towards loss of filial consortium.

Thus, the compensation which the appellants are entitled to is as under:
Amount Sl No. Compensation in Rs.
 1 Loss of dependency 23,43,600-00
2 Funeral expenses 16,500-00  3 Loss of estate 16,500-00
4 Loss of filial consortium 44,000-00  Total 24,20,600-00 Gangamma vs The Manager on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49729560/

Thus, the enhancement will be Rs.31,600/- (Rs.24,20,600/- -
Rs.23,89,000/-).

Thus, the appeal is disposed of with the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:37448 ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The compensation that is awarded by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Hassan, through orders in MVC No.873/2022 dated 02.09.2023 is enhanced by Rs.31,600/-.
(iii) The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
(iv) Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit enhanced sum within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
